\par\smallskip\noindent
\textsuperscript{a}~HEAT04: ARCH26 ran a new Krylov verification of CORA, not in CORA v2026.1.0; CORA++ runs the reach of CORA's ARCH23 script with a time step of 0.001. \\
\textsuperscript{b}~RND01--06: the report's instances are generated on the competition server; CORA++ runs the files of CORA's repeatability package (RND06: generated by us in their style), so the speedups (in parentheses) are indicative and left out of the medians. \\
\textsuperscript{c}~PLAN01, BRKNP01: the report verifies them with another setup than CORA's ARCH23 script, which does not verify them, neither in MATLAB nor in CORA++ (\ddag). \\
\textsuperscript{d}~LOVO25: CORA++ gives a sound verdict; CORA's script sets the result to true without a test. \\
\textsuperscript{e}~Unicycle: with the disturbance $w$ of the specification. \\
\textsuperscript{f}~DP less-robust: CORA++ splits the initial set (depth 14). \\
\textsuperscript{g}~Docking: UNKNOWN for CORA, JuliaReach and CORA++. \\
\textsuperscript{h}~CartPole*: the initial set of the specification; CORA's time is for 0.4 times its radius (\dag). \\
\textsuperscript{i}~CORA++ runs the 13 boxes of the initial set of CVDP23 and the pieces of a split initial set (DP less-robust, QUAD, NAV standard, CartPole*) on 8 threads. \\
\dag~Not counted: the report states another problem (JuliaReach discrete-time: time points only; immrax: continuous feedback instead of sample-and-hold; KeYmaera X and PRoTECT: a simplified or another property). \\
\S~Not counted: the tool's ARCH-COMP26 repeatability code solves another problem than the report states (JuliaReach: DTN, TRAF22, LALO20, LOVO25; CROWN-Reach: Single Pendulum, Attitude Control). \\
\ddag~Not counted: the verdict is UNKNOWN or not the expected one.
